newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks end week on flat note.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks end week on flat note.

text.p: Cyprus equities ended the week unchanged as high volumes of previous sessions was countered with a correction mid-week, analysts said on Friday.
"We had eight days of the market going up and in mid week there was a correction of the market," said Stavros Agrotis, senior trader with CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation.
The 43-share Cyprus Stock Exchange general index closed on Friday at 76.50, steady on last week's close of 76.48 points.
The bulk of transactions this week were absorbed by Bank of Cyprus ordinary shares and Bank of Cyprus nil paid rights. Agrotis said shares were trading at attractive levels.
"It is at this time that foreign investors should enter the market. It is cheap and there are plenty of very good buying opportunities," he said.
In a weekly technical analysis CISCO says the market has been bullish in the last few trading sessions as the short term, nine day moving average is up.
"I see the market moving in positive territory in the next few days. There is a climate of euphoria linked to prospects on the Cyprus problem," said Christodoulos Ellinas, a parter at Share Link.
United Nations-sponsored talks are due to start between the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities of the island on July 9 in an effort to speed up attempts to reunite Cyprus.
Turkey invaded its northern third in 1974 after a brief coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then in power in Greece.

Banking stocks closed the week 0.59 percent lower, at 84.92 points. Bank of Cyprus shares were trading at 295.5, down four cents from last week. Nil paid rights of the bank were trading at 95.5 from 99.5 last week.
Shares of Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 307.5, down one cent from last week while fully paid Hellenic Bank shares were trading at 280.5, steady on last week.
Universal Savings Bank shares jumped nine cents, closing at 181.
Insurance company Universal Life closed the week at 458 from 466 last week. Panuropean Insurance was steady at 101.5 and Interamerican was trading at 92.5, also steady on last week.
Blue chip cement stocks Vassiliko shares inched half a cent higher to 159.5, and Cyprus Cement shares closed at 248, one cent down from last week.
Beer and wine manufacturer KEO shares were trading at 110, up eight cents from last week.
"Some brokers are buying KEO stocks and this is pushing the price up, I don't think there is anything more to it," one broker said.
Shares in national carrier Cyprus Airways were trading at 32.8 cents from 29.7 last week.
